environment: R7 qualification venv (CPython 3.11.3, pyreadstat 1.3.6) read-only; synthetic carriers written under /tmp only

synthetic_carriers.origin: pyreadstat.write_sav on a literal hand-made frame — NOT survey data

tests.note: bytes exceed file size because ReadStat re-reads regions; the bridge is the only byte source

tests.test: naive broker exposing only .read/.seek returning raw file semantics
tests.result: FAILED: ReadstatError 'Unable to seek within file'
tests.significance: the compiled reader imposes real seek/tell semantics on the object — a toy broker is not sufficient; the seam expects a genuine seekable stream. A governed implementation must supply a correct tell() (pyobject_seek_handler returns file_obj.tell())

tests.test: pure io.BytesIO (no file descriptor, no path)
tests.significance: STRONGEST control-flow confirmation: with no path and no fd there is nothing for a compiled path-open to open, so all bytes provably arrived via the Python bridge

tests.result: all succeed (metadataonly rows=0; row_limit=1 -> 1 row; row_offset=1,row_limit=1 -> 1 row)
tests.significance: the broker route supports the bounded/budgeted read options the contract needs

tests.test: observed I/O vs usecols, SAV and DTA, 4000 rows
tests.result: IDENTICAL read counts and IDENTICAL byte totals with and without usecols; only the returned column count changes
tests.significance: DECISIVE for Part B: usecols is a pure POST-READ projection filter in pyreadstat 1.3.6. It changes the returned frame, not the physical read. It therefore cannot by itself realise the contract's separate 'selected-column read' account — see 04

pre_operation_ceiling_test.question: can a read/byte ceiling refuse BEFORE the excess operation executes, with loud failure?
pre_operation_ceiling_test.finding: NOT BY RAISING. The bridge's read handler is `try: data = file_obj.read(nbyte) ... except: return -1` (pyx:875-887) — a BARE except that converts ANY broker exception into a -1 return.

measured_failure_modes.mode: broker raises RuntimeError past the cap
measured_failure_modes.observed: PROCESS HANGS (no return within 12s; had to be killed)
measured_failure_modes.cause: the bare except returns -1 and the compiled reader retries indefinitely

measured_failure_modes.mode: broker returns b'' (premature EOF) past the cap
measured_failure_modes.observed: ReadstatError: 'Unable to read from file' — LOUD, prompt
ReadstatError 'Unable to read from file' at every cap — LOUD, no silent truncation

pre_operation_ceiling_test.safe_pattern: enforce the ceiling by returning a premature EOF (b''), never by raising inside read(). Raising must be reserved for OUTSIDE the bridge (e.g. before the read call is issued, or after it returns).
pre_operation_ceiling_test.why_loud: ReadStat knows the expected extent from the metadata it already parsed, so a short read is detected as an error rather than accepted as a legitimate end of data
pre_operation_ceiling_test.caveat: this is an empirical property of 1.3.6 on these two formats and these carriers; it is NOT a documented guarantee and must be re-tested on any version/format change

claim_verdicts.read_byte_ceilings_can_be_pre_operation: YES, but only via premature EOF — raising HANGS
claim_verdicts.loud_failure_rather_than_truncated_succe: YES on SAV and DTA with the EOF pattern; NO with the raising pattern (hang)

material_caveats_for_the_implementation: a toy broker without correct seek/tell fails outright
raising inside the broker hangs the reader — the ceiling pattern must be premature EOF
chunked reading cannot be driven by a single reused broker object (see 03)
